items.definition:
to give an unofficial name or nickname to; to replace the dialogue or sound in a film or video with a different language or sound
They decided to dub the foreign film into English.

experience or be subjected to
The building will undergo major renovations next year.

place or arrange in a straight line
Make sure the wheels are properly aligned.

move (something) from its proper or usual position; take the place of
The new factory will displace many local workers.

to have a specified beginning; to create or initiate something
The custom originated in ancient Egypt.

get back
Can you retrieve my keys from the car?

express strong feelings
She needed to vent her frustration.

control; limit
The government is trying to curb inflation.

separate; unfasten
Please detach the coupon from the bottom of the page.

take a risk; bet money
He decided to gamble all his savings on the stock market.

put or keep in prison
The judge decided to imprison the criminal for ten years.

fail to care for properly
Don't neglect your studies before the exam.

to inhabit or live in
The island was populated by a small community.

stop or cause to stop; delay
The car engine stalled at the traffic light.

make minor changes to (a text) in order to make it fairer or more accurate
They voted to amend the constitution.

begin; start
The ceremony will commence at 10 AM.

pay (someone) for work performed or to make up for a loss
They offered to compensate him for the damages.

to create or shape (a metal object) by heating it in a fire or furnace and beating or hammering it; to produce a fraudulent copy or imitation of (a document, signature, banknote, or work of art)
The blacksmith used a hammer to forge the iron.

to overcome and take control of (a place or people) by military force
The army managed to conquer the enemy territory.

to represent by a drawing, painting, or other art form
The painting depicts a scene from ancient mythology.

expose (one's country, a group, or a person) to danger by treacherously giving information to an enemy
He felt betrayed by his closest friend.

to make a short, high-pitched ringing sound; to send a brief electronic message
The microwave pinged when it finished.

to bounce back; to recover
The ball rebounded off the wall.

to order someone to come
The principal decided to summon the student's parents.

to make a sudden, small movement
His eye began to twitch nervously.

to remove a veil or covering; to reveal
The company will unveil its new product next month.

to increase speed
The car accelerated quickly on the highway.

to wait for
We eagerly await your response.

make (a bill or other proposal) law
Congress will enact new legislation next month.

enroll or be enrolled in the armed services
He decided to enlist in the army after high school.

combine or cause to combine to form a single entity
The two companies decided to merge.

to break into many pieces
The glass vase fell and shattered on the floor.

to bring to an end
The company decided to terminate his contract.

to enter a country or region with armed forces
The army planned to invade the neighboring territory.

to come before
A short introduction will precede the main presentation.

to wander off
Don't stray too far from the path.

bend (a limb or joint); contract (a muscle)
He began to flex his muscles to show off his strength.

to place or arrange
The company positioned itself strategically in the market.

to regain, to recover
She hopes to regain her strength after the illness.

to resemble, to look like
The child strongly resembles his father.

to grow or develop well or vigorously
The plants thrive in warm, sunny conditions.

to hide something
She tried to conceal her true feelings.

Come together again after a period of separation.
The family was overjoyed to reunite after the war.

Make great efforts to achieve or obtain something.
We must strive for excellence in everything we do.

to give special importance or prominence to something
The teacher wanted to emphasize the importance of reading.

to happen again
The problem tends to recur every spring.

praise enthusiastically and publicly
The critics acclaimed the new play.

comprehend
It's difficult to comprehend the full extent of the damage.

contaminate
The spilled chemicals could contaminate the water supply.

expel
The school decided to expel the student for cheating.

to leave someone in a place from which they cannot get away
The car broke down, leaving us stranded on the highway.

prevent (a person or place) from having or using something
Lack of sleep can deprive you of energy.

introduce (a liquid, especially a drug or vaccine) into the body with a syringe
The doctor will inject the vaccine into your arm.

arouse the curiosity or interest of; fascinate
The mystery novel truly intrigued me.

to control or influence skillfully, especially in an unfair way
He tried to manipulate the situation to his advantage.

to deliver a religious sermon or address
The minister will preach about forgiveness on Sunday.

estimate too low
Don't underestimate the power of a good book.

to represent something as being larger, better, or worse than it really is
Don't exaggerate; it wasn't that bad.

to bring back to life or consciousness
The paramedics tried to revive the unconscious man.

to astonish or shock (someone) so that they are temporarily unable to react
The news of his resignation stunned everyone in the office.

to become larger or rounder in size, typically as a result of an accumulation of fluid or air
Her ankle began to swell after she twisted it.

to surprise greatly
His talent continues to astonish me.

to make or become less
The pain began to diminish after an hour.

to live in a particular place
Many elderly people reside in this quiet neighborhood.
